slides.say: A, B, C and D represent different digits, and each of them is a prime number. Given: A B plus B C is equal to C D. C is equal to what?

Each letter is a different prime digit. We'll solve it by testing the choices for C. First write the addition vertically. Now list the prime digits: two, three, five and seven. There are four letters, so all four digits must be used.

C is the tens digit of the sum. We add A and B in the tens column, and there may also be a carried one. Could C be two or three? The smallest sum of two different prime digits is two plus three, which is five. A carry would only add more. So C cannot be two or three. Choice numbers two and three are out.

Now test C is seven. In the ones column, we add B plus seven to get the last digit D. If B is two, we get nine, which is not prime. If B is three, we get ten, ending in zero, which is not prime either. So B would have to be five. Five plus seven is twelve, giving D is two and a carried one. The tens column then says A plus five plus one is seven. That would make A one, but one is not prime. So C cannot be seven. This choice is out.

That leaves five as the only possible value of C. In the tens column, A and B can be two and three, adding to five. Check which goes in B. With B is two, the ones column gives two plus five is seven. That is the remaining prime digit for D, and there is no carry. So A is three, B is two, and D is seven.
The addition is thirty-two plus twenty-five equals fifty-seven. It works, and C is five. Choice number four is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
